dissent: The inherited note's 'distinct append-0/1/2 requests' justification under-describes the real premise: keys are index-scoped and fixture-blind (s_domain.py:48), equal-position-fork (s_domain.py:98) relies on a cross-fixture collision, and append-duplicate-lost-reply (s_domain.py:104) replays a key across restart; lookup equivalence stands on the unique-key invariant over all compared states, not on setup distinctness.

Both independent audits pick rows[0] first-match, so under a hypothetical duplicate-key state the B side would fail as a ledger mismatch (a_audit.py:31) rather than as a diagnosed lookup divergence; equivalence is only as strong as the uniqueness premise itself.
findings: Guard order is identical in all five derivations: owner -> receipt lookup -> incarnation -> pause -> registration -> position -> attempt -> scope -> commit (s_inclusive.py:36-53, s_split.py:41-62, batch-06/guard_a.py:37-54, batch-06/guard_b.py:38-59, s_audit.py:56-79, batch-06/guard_audit.py:37-60).

Lookup asymmetry is real code, not style: first-match next() at s_inclusive.py:38 and guard_a.py:39, and rows[0] first-match in both audits (s_audit.py:66-70, guard_audit.py:47-51), versus last-match dict.get at s_split.py:44 and guard_b.py:41. Decisions agree iff every request key has at most one stored row.

INV-APPEND (conditional invariant per reachable compared state): (a) request keys unique, len({r[0]})==len(append_receipts); (b) each row (req,(caller,boot,i,raw),(req,rev,i,h)) satisfies append_log[i]==raw and h==sha256(canon(raw)); (c) source_revision covers attempts+receipts+registration. Exactly the audited assertions at s_audit.py:18-23.

Proof obligation (induction over admitted transitions): append_receipts is written only by the commit branch (s_inclusive.py:51-53, s_split.py:59-62, guard_a.py:52-54, guard_b.py:56-59), which fires only when the same guard's lookup missed; delegated Q steps cannot touch it because project()/baseline select q-fields only (s_domain.py:23-24, s_inclusive.py:74, s_split.py:83-88) and adapter journals are EXTRA-key projections of guard output (guard_a.py:76, guard_b.py:88, a_inclusive.py:9-10).

Falsifiable idempotency clauses: replay of admitted (request,body) -> 'append:duplicate' with stored receipt and no ledger mutation (s_inclusive.py:41-43, s_split.py:46-48); same request with different body -> 'append-id-conflict'; foreign caller -> 'wrong-append-owner' before any lookup (s_inclusive.py:40, s_split.py:45, caller set at s_domain.py:51); no-receipt plus boot!=source_generation -> 'stale-append-incarnation' (s_inclusive.py:44, s_split.py:49).

Reachable consequence: because the lookup branch precedes the incarnation check, a post-restart replay of a pre-restart append returns 'duplicate' with the old-revision receipt, not 'stale-append-incarnation' (ordering at s_inclusive.py:41-44; profile append-duplicate-lost-reply, s_domain.py:104).

Divergence clause (falsifies unconditional equivalence): any reachable state containing two rows with equal r[0] but different body or receipt makes first-vs-last picks disagree on decision or append_reply. This is a hypothetical malformed state: no supplied branch can construct it.

Request keys are fixture-blind: 'append-'+index (s_domain.py:48), variant-suffixed only for 'fresh' (s_domain.py:56); cross-fixture same-index appends collide and yield 'append-id-conflict' (profile equal-position-fork, s_domain.py:98); 'new-boot' only alters the offered body (s_domain.py:57).

Smallest decisive check: mirror the unique-key and receipt-shape assertions (s_audit.py:18-22) onto adapter journals inside a_audit (today only qa.invariant(after['core']) at a_audit.py:36; journal correctness rests solely on exact ledger equality at a_audit.py:31), then run the existing complete audit over the packet's typed histories; necessity of the premise is shown by the single malformed duplicate-row counterexample above.
limitations: Source inspection only; no execution, imports, or reducer runs, per brief. All reachability claims are branch-exhaustion arguments over the supplied files, not machine-checked over all orders.
The unique-key invariant is conditional: it is asserted per checked transition (s_audit.py:18), not proved over the full admitted order domain or independently for adapter journals.

Fixture contents, q_inclusive/q_split/q_audit internals, and adapter_traces.py were not in the packet; whether a given setup actually admits index i (hence duplicate-vs-stale outcomes) is an unchecked premise.
Mutant escape hatches and the collect-path lower-bound asymmetry (s_inclusive.py:57 vs s_split.py:68) were excluded as test-only/out-of-scope.
summary: Derived a source-backed conditional invariant (INV-APPEND) and proof obligation for setup-append idempotency and the first-vs-last receipt-lookup discrepancy between the inclusive/A-side and split/B-side sources. Lookup equivalence holds iff append_receipts request keys are unique; uniqueness is an audited per-transition assertion, not yet a proven all-orders invariant.
